Let me analyze the screenshot. It shows a zen-panel remote control app for Android, controlling a desktop screen (YouTube). Issues I can see:

1. The top status bar / address bar: there's a floating "video player" widget (the anime thumbnail) overlapping the browser URL bar area. That looks like a floating PIP (picture-in-picture) video overlay that's positioned incorrectly — it covers the browser toolbar.

2. The desktop screen content is rendered but split — there's a duplicated/ghost content. The right side of the screen (from x≈365 to 720) shows a mirrored/cut version of the left side. It looks like the screen stream is being drawn twice or there are rendering artifacts. Actually looking more closely: the left portion shows YouTube page, the right portion shows a mirrored duplicate. There's a vertical scrollbar-like line at x≈370. Hmm, this could be the "split view" issue.

Actually wait. Let me reconsider. The whole content area from y≈210 to y≈1270 shows the remote screen. The content appears... the left half shows the YouTube page (hamburger menu, YouTube logo, Sign in, Explore, Shopping, Music, Movies, Show more, More from YouTube). The right half at x>365 shows a mirrored version of that same content but offset — the scrollbar at x≈370, then blank white, then a hand cursor, then "Music" tooltip overlapping. So it looks like there are TWO renderings of the same frame side by side, i.e., the image is being rendered twice with a seam. That's a critical rendering bug — the frame is being tiled/stretched incorrectly.

3. The "Music" tooltip (hover tooltip) is rendered as a black box with white text at (225,1000) — that's part of the actual screen content (YouTube's nav tooltip). Fine.

4. The blue circle at (207, 970) is the touch indicator. OK.

5. Bottom control bar: "СЕНСОР · тяни — курсор, тап — клик, два тапа — двойной" hint panel, ЛКМ, ПКМ buttons, and D-pad arrows. The D-pad arrow buttons: up arrow at top-right, left/down/right in a weird arrangement. Layout looks odd — up on top right, then left and right in the middle row, and down below-left. Should be a proper D-pad diamond. That's a UI layout bug.

6. The floating widget (anime video thumbnail) — that's likely a "preview thumbnail" or an overlay from the app. It overlaps the URL bar. It has an X button at (686, 1281) to close. This might be the screen's floating window preview.

219:             runCatching {

221:                     setNotificationVisibility(
222:                         DownloadManager.Request.VISIBILITY_VISIBLE_NOTIFY_COMPLETED
223:                     )
224:                     // Android guesses filenames from URL+MIME and mangles real
225:                     // extensions (apk → .bin / .ts1). Use the server's filename
226:                     // from Content-Disposition and store into Downloads with it.
227:                     val name = dispositionFilename(contentDisposition) ?: urlFilename(url)

244:     // Prefer RFC 5987 filename*=, then the legacy filename=. This preserves
245:     // compound names such as app.tar.xz and release.apk instead of letting
246:     // DownloadManager invent a .bin/.ts extension from the MIME type.
247:     private fun dispositionFilename(cd: String?): String? {
248:         if (cd.isNullOrBlank()) return null
249:         val encoded = Regex("""filename\*\s*=\s*UTF-8''([^;]+)""", RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE)
250:             .find(cd)?.groupValues?.getOrNull(1)
251:         val plain = Regex("""filename\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]+)"|([^;]+))""", RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE)
252:             .find(cd)?.let { it.groupValues[1].ifBlank { it.groupValues[2] } }
253:         var name = (encoded?.let { runCatching { URLDecoder.decode(it.trim(), "UTF-8") }.getOrNull() }
254:             ?: plain)?.trim()?.trim('"')
255:         if (name.isNullOrBlank() || name.equals("download", ignoreCase = true)) return null
256:         name = name.replace(Regex("""[/\\:*?"<>|%{}]"""), "_").trim()

293:             lower.endsWith(".png") -> "image/png"
294:             lower.endsWith(".jpg") || lower.endsWith(".jpeg") -> "image/jpeg"
295:             lower.endsWith(".webp") -> "image/webp"
296:             lower.endsWith(".pdf") -> "application/pdf"
297:             lower.endsWith(".mp4") -> "video/mp4"

--- .github/workflows/js-syntax.yml

 name: JS syntax
 
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main]
     paths: ["agent/**", "desktop/**", "npm-hub/**", "hub/**", "tools/**", ".github/workflows/**"]
   pull_request:
     paths: ["agent/**", "desktop/**", "npm-hub/**", "hub/**", "tools/**", ".github/workflows/**"]
 
 jobs:
   check:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     timeout-minutes: 5
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with: { node-version: "20" }
       - name: Syntax-check the agent and hub
         run: |
           node --check agent/zen-agent.js
           node --check agent/local-models.js
           node --check agent/capabilities.js
           node --check agent/oc-gateway.js
           node --check agent/github-api.js
           node --check agent/cloud-store.js
           python3 - <<'PY'
           import pathlib, re, subprocess, sys
           html = pathlib.Path("agent/hub/index.html").read_text()
           m = re.search(r"<script>\s*(.*?)\s*</script>\s*</body>", html, re.S)
           if not m:
               sys.exit("hub/index.html: no inline script")
           pathlib.Path("/tmp/hub.js").write_text(m.group(1))
           subprocess.check_call(["node", "--check", "/tmp/hub.js"])
           print("ok")
           PY
       - name: Syntax-check the desktop shell
         run: |
           node --check desktop/main.js
           node --check desktop/preload.js
           node --check desktop/panel-store.js
           node desktop/test-panel-store.js
       - name: Syntax-check npm-hub
         run: |
           node --check npm-hub/src/server.js
           node --check npm-hub/src/tunnel.js
           node --check npm-hub/src/models/manager.js
           # Both live under src/ and both run inside the hub process - a typo
           # in either is a crash at boot, and neither was ever checked here.
           node --check npm-hub/src/vnc-keepalive.js
           node --check npm-hub/src/handoff.js
           for f in npm-hub/src/storage/*.js; do node --check "$f"; done
           node --check npm-hub/public/desktop-app.js
           node --check npm-hub/public/mobile-app.js
           node --check npm-hub/public/remote-audio.js
           node --check npm-hub/public/term-app.js
+          node --check npm-hub/public/term-mouse.js
+          node --check npm-hub/public/sw.js
           for f in tools/*.sh; do bash -n "$f"; done

Excellent! This is very informative. The terminal ALREADY has a rich touch layer:
- Swipe = wheel scroll (`fireWheel`) — works.
- Long press (550ms) = select word.
- Tap = focus (show keyboard).
- Right-click (contextmenu) = select word.

And there are helpers `termCellAt(term, x, y)` and `termSelectWordAt(term, x, y)`! So cell↔pixel mapping already exists.

So the terminal's touch handling is already good. The missing piece is exactly what the user asks: the Экран-style control (pad + ЛКМ/ПКМ + wheel) — a *control bar*.

Given `termCellAt` exists, the crosshair aiming via long-press already exists implicitly (selection). So I don't need a crosshair overlay for aiming — I can reuse the existing tap/long-press mechanics:

New bar semantics (final, consistent with the existing touch layer):
- **СЕНСОР pad** (big): drag = колесо (scroll) — the same `fireWheel` path, but now with a large surface, plus tap = шаг, double tap = страница. This is a *reliable, big* version of what the old 62×58 pad did, and matches the Экран pad visually.
- **ЛКМ / ПКМ**: send real mouse press/release to the app at the **aimed cell** (the last cell the user aimed at — from the existing long-press/tap position or the center by default), with **hold-to-drag** support: while held, moving the pad moves the aim → selection in vim/less. Dimmed + note when the app hasn't enabled mouse reporting.
- **Wheel ▲▼◀▶**: scroll / wheel events.
- **Aim**: a crosshair overlay that shows where ЛКМ/ПКМ will click, positioned by a **tap on the terminal** (reuse: on tap, also set the aim cell) and by pad drags while a button is held.

The crosshair: add an absolutely-positioned marker div inside `.term-wrap` at the aimed cell. On tap in the terminal (`setupTermTouch.onEnd` when `!scrolled`), set the aim cell → show the marker. That's a tiny addition to `setupTermTouch` and no interception of existing behavior. 

Then the bar's ЛКМ/ПКМ press → dispatch synthetic mousedown at the marker; while held + pad drag → mousemove; release → mouseup. If no aim was ever set, default to the terminal center.

This is a solid, coherent feature. Let me now also decide: do I keep the old `.term-scroll` cluster and `#term-arrows`? The user said "заместь прошлого неработающего вовсе" → replace. So:
- Remove the old `.term-scroll` cluster (pad/wheel/handle) — replaced by the new bar.
- Remove `#term-arrows` from mobile.html (its ▲◀▶▼ are duplicated by the wheel diamond; Tab/Enter// need a home) → put Tab/Enter/`/` into the new bar as a small key column? Hmm, that makes the bar crowded on a 360px-wide phone: pad (flex) + [ЛКМ,ПКМ] 74px + wheel 88px = 162px fixed, leaving ~180px for the pad. Adding a key column (another 60px) leaves 120px for the pad — too narrow.

Better: keep Tab/Enter accessible where they already are — the soft keyboard has Tab/Enter, and `sendEscape` exists in the topbar. Hmm, but `#term-arrows`' Enter/Tab/`/` are handy.

Option: keep `#term-arrows` as-is (it's a static overlay with Tab/Enter//) and only replace the broken `.term-scroll` cluster with the new bar. But then the terminal has two floating clusters again (arrows at bottom-right + the new bar at the bottom). Conflict.

Option: move Tab/Enter/`/` into the terminal topbar `.term-controls`? It's already crowded (9 buttons, horizontally scrollable).

Option: Put them in the new bar, but merge ЛКМ/ПКМ/Tab/Enter into ONE column of 4 small buttons (like the Экран bar's `.lm-buttons` but taller):
```
[ ЛКМ ]
[ ПКМ ]
[ Tab ]
[ ⏎  ]
```
and the wheel diamond. Width: buttons col 74px + wheel 88px = 162px, pad gets the rest (~190px on a 360px screen). That works — the pad is still much bigger than the old 62px. And `/` can go... drop it (the soft keyboard has it, and the topbar has paste). Hmm, `/` is used a lot in a shell (paths). But `Tab` completes paths. Fine, drop `/`... Actually the topbar has a "Вставить" (paste) button, so text entry is covered.

Wait — I should double check: does removing `#term-arrows` break anything else? The test q1/q2/q3 count buttons. I'll update the test.

Also `#term-arrows` uses `sendKey()` which sends to `activeTab` — fine.

Hmm, actually — hold on. Let me reconsider removing `#term-arrows`. The user said "заместь прошлого неработающего вовсе" (instead of the previous completely non-working one). Singular "одного". Which one is "the previous non-working one"? Both are old. The `.term-scroll` cluster is the one described in code comments as "Виртуальная мышь" (the previous attempt at this very control) — that's clearly "the previous one" being replaced, since the new thing IS "the same control". `#term-arrows` is a different, older thing (arrows/Tab/Enter) that likely works.

Decision: replace the `.term-scroll` cluster with the new bar; KEEP `#term-arrows`... but they'd overlap at the bottom-right. Unless the new bar sits at the bottom and `#term-arrows` is removed...

parts.text:
Wait: `attachTermScroll` is called after `fitTerm(tab)` in createTerm, so at first fit there's no bar yet. But mount() itself calls paint() at the end, so the mark gets positioned. ✓

But there's an ordering issue: `attachTermScroll` is called before `connect()` and before xterm has rendered content. `metrics(st)` needs `.xterm-screen` with a non-zero rect. xterm's DOM is created at `open()`, and `.xterm-screen` exists with size after the first render/fit. Since `fitTerm` ran before mount, the screen should have a size. And if not, `paint` runs on the first scroll/buffer-change/resize. To be safe, let me also call `st.upd()` on a `requestAnimationFrame` after mount, and on `term.onRender`. Simplest: in mount, `setTimeout(function(){ paint(st); }, 0)` plus a one-shot on the next render. Let me add a `term.onRender(function(){ paint(st); })` subscription — that fires on every render (could be frequent, but paint is cheap-ish: 2 getBoundingClientRect + style writes). Hmm, onRender fires very often during heavy output. The mark only needs repainting when the viewport scrolls (buffer change / scroll) or on resize. I already subscribe to viewport scroll + buffer change + window resize. That covers it.

Let me add a `setTimeout(paint, 0)` and a `setTimeout(paint, 300)` for safety after mount. Cheap.

Also: `tab.scroll.destroy()` on close — check the close path calls it. And `attachTermScroll` returning the mount handle `{upd, destroy}` ✓.

parts.text:
Two failures:

1. "Tab goes to the PTY" — the data IS `\t` but my check compares `s.d === '\t'` where the seen value is the literal string... The output shows `{"t":"send","d":"\\t"}` which in JSON means the string contains a backslash + t (2 chars), not a tab! So `getAttribute('data-send')` returned the raw attribute value `\\t` (backslash backslash t) — because in the HTML string I wrote `data-send="\\t"`, and the browser does NOT process HTML entity/JS escapes in attribute values. So the attribute literally contains `\\t` (two backslashes + t). That's a BUG in my implementation!

Right: in the innerHTML string `'<button ... data-send="\\t" ...>'`, the JS string escape `\\t` produces the two characters `\t`... wait: in a JS single-quoted string, `'\\t'` is backslash + t (2 chars). So the HTML attribute is `data-send="\t"` (backslash + t, 2 chars) — not a TAB. And `getAttribute` returns `\t` as 2 chars (backslash, t). So Tab sends a literal backslash-t to the shell. BUG.

Fix: use `data-send="tab"` / `data-send="enter"` and map to real control chars in JS, or use `	` / `` HTML entities which the HTML parser converts. Cleanest: use named data attributes and a small map in JS:

```js
'<button class="tm-key" data-key="tab" ...>Tab</button>' +
'<button class="tm-key" data-key="enter" ...>⏎</button>' +
...
var KEYS = { tab: '\t', enter: '\r' };
if (typeof st.send === 'function') st.send(KEYS[b.getAttribute('data-key')] || '');
```

That's readable and avoids escape confusion.

2. "a tap aims the cursor" — the touchend handler. My test dispatches an Event with `changedTouches` assigned. In jsdom, `new window.Event('touchend')` then Object.assign to add changedTouches — assigning to a plain Event object works (it's a JS object). Hmm, but the handler checks `p.moved > 12 || Date.now() - p.at > 700` — `st.tap` is null because I never dispatched `touchstart` on termEl! So the handler returns early. My test is wrong: I need to dispatch touchstart first. Let me fix the test to dispatch touchstart → touchend.

Also `metrics(st)` returns null in jsdom (rect 0) → `setAimFrom` returns early without setting the aim! So the aim can't be verified in jsdom unless I stub getBoundingClientRect. Let me stub `screen.getBoundingClientRect` to return a real rect (jsdom allows overriding the method on the element instance).

Let me stub: `screen.getBoundingClientRect = () => ({left:0, top:0, width: 800, height: 480, right:800, bottom:480})` and `termEl.getBoundingClientRect` too (for the wrap offset in paintMark). Also `wrap.getBoundingClientRect`.

With cw = 800/80 = 10, ch = 480/24 = 20: a tap at (50,50) → col 5, row 2. 

Then the mark positioning will also work, and I can assert the mark's left/top. Let me also verify the mark becomes visible (display '').

parts.text:
The diff looks clean. A few remaining considerations:

1. The old `#term-arrows` also had a `/` key button. It's gone; the topbar has a paste button and the soft keyboard has `/`. Acceptable. But wait — the old arrows also provided ▲◀▶▼ as *key* sends (arrow keys for the shell/shell navigation, e.g. bash history with ↑). Now ▲▼ = wheel scroll, and ◀▶ = horizontal wheel. So **shell history navigation (↑/↓) is lost from the on-screen buttons**! That's a real regression for phone users: pressing ▲ in the old pad gave you `↑` = previous command in bash.

Hmm. That's important. On the Экран tab, ▲▼ are the wheel. But in a terminal, users expect ▲/▼ to be arrow keys for history/TUI navigation... but the pad/wheel semantics is what the user asked for ("это же управление").

The soft keyboard has an arrow bar? Android's soft keyboard usually doesn't have arrow keys (Gboard has a bottom-right ">" for symbols/hidden layout with arrows sometimes). Hmm. This could be a real usability loss.

Solution that keeps both: make the wheel arrows do "wheel" by default but... no, ambiguity is bad.

Better solution: keep a separate small row of arrow KEYS in the keys column? The keys column already has ЛКМ, ПКМ, Tab, Enter. Adding ▲▼ there = 6 buttons in 54px → 9px each. Too small.

Alternative: in the alt-buffer (vim/top/opencode) case, xterm's wheel → arrow keys, so the wheel already acts as arrows inside TUIs. For a plain shell, the wheel scrolls the scrollback (what you want when reading output), and history needs ↑ — reachable via... the `↑` in the mobile browser's own UI? No.

Hmm. Let me think about the actual user need: they use agents (opencode) in this terminal, and the shell. Losing ↑/↓ history buttons is a real cost.

Compromise: the wheel ▲▼ long... no.

Option: put ▲▼ key-buttons in the TOPBAR as `↑`/`↓` next to Esc (there's a `.term-controls` row with Esc). The topbar already has: ⏹ Esc 📋 ⧉ ⟲ − % + ⟲ 🖱 ⛶ = 10 buttons. Adding ↑ ↓ = 12; the row is horizontally scrollable (`overflow-x:auto`). On a 390px phone at 36px+6px gap = ~42px per button → 12 buttons = 504px > 390. It scrolls, so it's usable but adds friction.

Better idea: the hint is that the wheel diamond's ▲▼ in the *terminal* context should send arrow keys when the app is NOT in mouse mode and we're in... no, too magic.

Cleanest: since the terminal bar's wheel is for scrolling, add a compact "history" pair inside the pad area? No.

Let me reconsider the layout: the keys column (86px) holds 4 buttons stacked: ЛКМ(26px), ПКМ(26px), Tab(19px), Enter(19px). I could make it 2 rows × 2 cols: [ЛКМ][ПКМ] / [Tab][Enter] — that's what I described earlier. Then I could add a 3rd row [▲][▼] for arrow keys. 3 rows × 18px = 54px. And the column becomes 2×44=88px wide. Wheel is 78px. Total fixed = 166px, leaving ~200px for the pad on a 390px screen. That works and keeps ▲▼ (wheel) plus ↑↓ (keys) distinct.

Hmm, but is that too busy? The bar would be: pad | [ЛКМ][ПКМ] / [Tab][Enter] / [↑][↓] | wheel diamond | ✕

Wait — ↑↓ keys AND ▲▼ wheel adjacent to each other is confusing. Maybe label the key buttons as "⌃历史"...

Alternative cleaner approach: drop the separate Tab/Enter buttons (the soft keyboard has both, and Tab is also what the wheel's... no).

Let me think about which is more valuable in a phone terminal:
1. Mouse buttons (ЛКМ/ПКМ) — the user explicitly asked for these.
2. Wheel ▲▼◀▶ — asked for.
3. Tab/Enter — very handy (no soft-keyboard arrows needed for these).

Since the user's request is explicitly "this same control" (pad + ЛКМ/ПКМ + wheel), and they described the old one as "неработающий вовсе", I'll provide the Экран control faithfully + Tab/Enter, AND keep ↑/↓ arrow keys available because dropping them is a regression. and the wheel diamond separately as ▲▼◀▶.

Hmm, ↑↓ vs ▲▼ side by side...

[ ↑   ][ ↓   ]
```
plus keep Tab/Enter... no, dropping Tab is bad for the shell.

Let me look at it from a different angle: the old control's ▲▼ sent `\x1b[A`/`\x1b[B` — which is EXACTLY what xterm's wheel does in alt-buffer mode. And in a plain shell, the wheel scrolls. The user has been using the old (broken) control, so they probably weren't relying on ↑↓.

Both badges (⟳ 5с and ♻ Перезапустить сессию) now sit above the bar, and `--tmouse-inset` is 99px (bar 91px + 8).

Hmm, the bar looks a bit tall here (91px) because the pad's min-height is 54px + padding 12 + ... In this demo the pad's hint wraps to 2 lines making the bar taller? The keys grid is 3 rows × ~26px + gaps = 86px → the bar height = 86 + 12 padding = 98. Right — the keys grid drives the height (3 rows), not the pad. Let me reduce: rows are `1fr` each in a grid whose height is determined by content... The grid's height is driven by the tallest item. `.tm-btn`/`.tm-key` have `flex:1 1 0` (from the shared rule) — in a grid, `flex` doesn't apply, so the height is content-based: font 11px + padding 0 + border → ~15px? But they render ~26px tall. Hmm, `.tmouse` is `display:flex; align-items:stretch`, so the `.tm-keys` grid stretches to the bar's height, and the grid's implicit rows are `auto`... I set `grid-auto-rows: 1fr` which in a stretched grid distributes the height equally → 3 rows over the bar's height.

The bar's height comes from the flex row: the tallest item. The pad has min-height 54px; the wheel is 3 rows × 24px + 6px gaps = 78px! So the wheel drives the height: 78px + 12 padding = 90px. Yes.

Is 90px too tall for a phone terminal? The Экран bar in the screenshot is ~190px tall on a 720px-wide screen (a scaled screenshot of a phone at ~390dp? The screenshot is 720px wide for a 390dp screen → 1.85x. So the Экран bar ≈ 190/1.85 ≈ 103dp tall!). So ~90dp for the terminal bar is comparable to the Экран one. That's consistent with "это же управление".

Still, let me trim it a bit: the wheel arrows are 24px tall; I could reduce to 22px and the gap to 2px → 70px. And the pad min-height 54 → 48. The keys grid will follow the bar height. Let's target ~78px total. Actually, since the user wants the same control and it looks good, I'll trim slightly: `.tm-arr{height:22px}`, `.tm-wheel{gap:2px}`, `.tm-mid{gap:2px}`, `.tm-keys{gap:3px}`. → wheel = 3*22+2*2 = 70; bar = 70+12 = 82px. Slightly better for a small terminal.

Let me also double check: with `.tm-keys` grid-auto-rows:1fr and 3 rows, each row = (82-12-2*3)/3 ≈ 21px — enough for 11px text. OK.

`sendWheel` returning true means the event was dispatched — xterm handles it. Note xterm's `_wheelPartialScroll` accumulates, so fractional deltas work nicely.

Another check: `aim(st)` is called in `aimPoint` — if `st.aim` is null it computes the default each time until metrics work. Fine.

A few observations:

1. `buttonDown` when `!st.mouseOn` sets the note. But the note is never restored to the default hint after the button is released. Once the user taps ЛКМ in a shell, the pad hint stays "приложение мышь не включило" forever (until the app enables the mouse). That's arguably fine/informative, but it'd be better to restore the default after a moment. Let me make `buttonUp` restore the default hint when the app still has no mouse, and also have a `defaultHint()` helper so the initial text isn't duplicated in two places.

2. `note()` in `watchModes` sets "мышь включена приложением — ЛКМ/ПКМ кликают" — this also persists. Should revert to the default when the app disables the mouse (DECRST) or... let me revert on the next `buttonUp` too. Simplest: keep a `st.mouseNote` and restore the default hint whenever `buttonUp` runs and no button is held.

Let me implement `defaultHint()`:
```js
function defaultHint(st) {
  return st.mouseOn
    ? 'СЕНСОР · тяни — колесо, с ЛКМ — курсор, тап по экрану — навести'
    : 'СЕНСОР · тяни — колесо, тап — шаг, два тапа — страница';
}
```
and in build(): `st.hint.textContent = defaultHint(st);` (st.mouseOn is false at build time).

And in buttonUp: `if (!heldMask(st) && !st.drag) note(st, defaultHint(st));`

Hmm, but during a drag with a held button we don't want to stomp the hint. The condition `!heldMask(st)` covers it.

3. `heldMask(st)` is used as the `buttons` value in sendMouse: mask 1 = left, 4 = right ✓ matches the MouseEvent.buttons bitmask.

4. In `buttonDown` for ПКМ I send `button: 2, buttons: 4` ✓.

Let me also reconsider: when the app has mouse mode ON and the user taps the pad (scroll mode), nothing is sent to the app except a wheel event — correct.

5. `paint` sets `.dim` on the buttons when `!st.mouseOn`. But `.tm-btn.dim{opacity:.38}` — combined with the hint, the user understands. Good.

Let me implement the hint restore.
